method: Read every run fn in the 17 modules registry() collects (crates/engine/src/cmd/*.rs; 389 ids, identical to the catalog) and followed each into its helpers (io.rs open_path/save_path, session.rs run/clipboard/ui_requests, wordcraft_proof add_word, references::update_fields, layout fields), then grepped the engine and every lower crate for std::fs, std::process, network, env and clipboard use and checked the workspace dependencies: the engine has no network, OS-clipboard or dialog crate, so its only I/O is the path reads/writes and the process spawn named in these rules, and its front-end effects exist only as ui_requests (checked against wordcraft's egui UI for what each one does). Commands whose whole effect is a UI request, a ViewState toggle or a preference are host; a dialog request queued only when a path/url/text param is missing, or an incidental pane flag, does not reclassify an in-document or path command; caller-chosen nested execution (macros, replay) is code, while fixed engine-chosen delegation takes its target's class; stubs are classed by what they reach when implemented. Limits: nothing was built or executed (readAloud's argument-injection risk is unverified), and layout reads installed fonts from fixed platform font folders for any command (crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs system_font_dirs), which no parameter can point at a path, so it is not counted as file.

rules.why: Typing, breaks and deletion edit the open document in memory (type_text, split_para, delete_selection); text.insert's AutoCorrect uses only the session's own word lists.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:450-491 autocorrect(): s.autocorrect_user + built-in AUTOCORRECT table

rules.why: Caret moves only change s.sel, using the in-memory layout for up/down/line/page.
Selection commands set s.sel from positions, text matches, same-formatting runs or inline objects in the document.
Undo/redo swap in-memory snapshots, find/replace run a size-limited regex over the document's paragraphs, and format-painter state lives in the session.
Character formatting rewrites run properties in the open document (format_range, or pending caret props); format.state is a query.
Paragraph formatting, lists, borders, tabs, sorting and numbering edit paragraph props and the document's numbering table in memory.
Create, modify, update, delete and list styles in the document's own style sheet (s.doc.styles).

Every view.* command toggles UI-only view state in s.view (zoom, view mode, panes, ruler, dark mode, page movement) or queues a window request (newWindow, split, zoom dialog) for the front end, and view.state reads that UI state back. None changes the document.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs:9-13 toggle(s.view), 15-71 specs, 58-67 ui_requests newWindow/split, 80-100 zoom
crates/engine/src/session.rs:34-57 ViewState, separate from the Document

rules.why: Pages, tables, shapes, text boxes, bookmarks, headers/footers, symbols, equations, cross-references, Quick Parts (session s.building_blocks) and the date (system clock) are built in memory; none of these reads a path or the network.
Margins, size, orientation, columns, breaks, line numbers, hyphenation and header/footer linking edit section properties and document settings.
Table edits change the in-memory table; table.formula is a bounded SUM/AVERAGE/COUNT/MAX/MIN/PRODUCT over neighbouring cells, and table.quick uses built-in data.
Comments, tracked changes, restrict editing, language tags, word count, and proofing against wordcraft_proof's embedded word lists and a built-in thesaurus, all on the open document.

file.open and file.newFromTemplate read any path with io::open_path; file.save, saveAs, saveTemplate and exportPdf write any path with io::save_path (writes a <path>.<ext>.tmp sibling, then renames); exportPng uses std::fs::write. file.save with no path writes to the session's current path s.path; without a path, open/save/saveAs only queue a dialog.
evidence: crates/engine/src/io.rs:43-51 open_path (fs::metadata, fs::read), 58-65 save_path (fs::write tmp + fs::rename)
crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:15-22 exportPdf, 92-106 open, 108-137 save/saveAs (s.path fallback), 139-150 exportPng fs::write

rules.why: Agent queries of the open document (structure, text, paragraph, selection, layout summary); document.setText replaces the body in memory.
Themes, theme fonts and colours, style sets, spacing, watermark, page colour and borders come from built-in tables and edit the document's styles and settings.

TOC, notes, captions, citations, bibliography, index and tables of figures/authorities are generated from the document; sources come from command params into s.doc.sources, never from a bibliography file.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs:14-95 specs, 210-231 sources() from params, 318-358 update_generated()

rules.why: Merge fields, rules, preview, record navigation and checks work on the in-session merge state (s.merge) and the document; envelopes and labels build a new in-memory document. Nothing sends mail: the emails kind is only a label.
Size, crop, alt text and image adjustments decode the picture from s.doc.media, transform it with the image crate (80 Mpx cap) and store a new PNG in the document.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs:32-173 specs, 374-393 adjust(), 395-405 reset() from s.originals

rules.why: Rotate, wrap, position, order and align change the selected object's float settings or bitmap in memory.
Fill, outline and shape kind of the selected shape object.
Header/footer navigation between section parts, and header/footer distances in section props.

tools.macros defines macros as arbitrary [{command, params}] lists and runs them through Session::run (up to 10,000 steps, any id including path and process commands); tools.recordMacro records later commands into such a macro. A deny-list on the outer id cannot see the steps.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:58-74 specs, 419-447 macros(): define, then s.run(id, params) per step
crates/engine/src/session.rs:331-336 recording captures every caret/select/mutating command

rules.why: Replays s.last_command, the last mutating command with its original params, through Session::run. That command can be insert.picture, insert.textFromFile, review.compare or mailings.finish with a path, set earlier by another caller or a macro step.
evidence: crates/engine/src/session.rs:337-339 last_command records every mutating id

rules.why: Spawns an OS process to speak up to 20,000 characters of document text: say on macOS, powershell -NoProfile -Command on Windows, spd-say or espeak on other Unix (audio output too). The text is one argv element with no --, so a paragraph starting with '-' reaches those tools as options.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:376, 781-826 read_aloud(): std::process::Command::new(say | powershell | spd-say | espeak)

rules.why: Stub: it only sets the status 'Researcher needs an online service' and returns available:false. Implemented, it queries an online research service.
Their only effect is to queue a dialog request (ui_requests open: font | paragraph) for the front end.
They toggle UI-only view flags in s.view (styles pane; show markup / display for review); the document is unchanged.

App preferences from File > Options: the user name stamped on comments, revisions and saves (s.author), AutoCorrect on/off and user entries, and check-spelling-as-you-type (s.view.proofing). wordcraft keeps them in session memory rather than a config file.
Both call wordcraft_proof::add_word, which inserts into a process-global user dictionary (static RwLock<HashSet>) shared by every session in the process; Ignore All is not document-scoped.
Stub: it only sets the status 'These settings will be used for new documents.' Implemented, it persists the current design as the app's default for new documents.

Each only queues a front-end request: print opens wordcraft's backstage Print page (a PDF export; there is no printer API anywhere), close makes the desktop app quit, options opens Options, and share opens the Save As dialog with a hint (no upload).
evidence: crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:179-199 close -> quit_requested; crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs:227-228 'Printing goes through a PDF'

rules.why: Stub: it sets a status and always fails with 'password encryption isn't available yet'. Implemented, it needs a password, which only a host-owned prompt may collect.
Stub in the engine: it toggles s.autosave, which nothing reads. Working AutoSave (wordcraft's UI, using its own flag) re-runs file.save to the open document's path every few seconds.
Replaces the open document with a template built in code by crate::sample (blank, sample, letter, resume, report); no file is read.
Metadata, reports and checks on the open document. file.inspect removes content through fixed review/insert commands, and file.protect only runs review.restrict (a document setting).
Save, restore and list snapshots kept in session memory (s.versions, at most 50); despite its label, file.recover reads no recovery directory.
With path they std::fs::read any file (all of it, before insert.picture's 200 MB check) and embed the bytes; base64 data avoids I/O. insert.picture with neither only queues the picture dialog.
insert.textFromFile parses any supported document at path with io::open_path and pastes its body; insert.object only runs insert.textFromFile with the same path.
With path they load the revised document via io::open_path and merge its text into the open document as tracked changes, which makes the file's contents readable; text avoids I/O.
With path it std::fs::reads any file as the CSV data source into s.merge, and mailings.editRecipients then returns those rows; csv or rows avoid I/O.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs:39-47 editRecipients returns headers and rows

rules.why: With path it writes the merged document via io::save_path; without it, it replaces the open document in memory.

Engine-internal clipboard: copy and cut store a Fragment plus a text mirror in the session (s.clipboard, s.clipboard_text), and paste takes caller-supplied text or that Fragment. Only the egui front end touches the OS clipboard.
evidence: crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs:146-147 the UI copies clipboard_text to the OS clipboard

rules.why: With params they search, move the caret, or set/read section props in the document. With none they also queue a dialog (ui_requests find / goto / pageSetup), which changes nothing else and can be discarded.
Stores the URL as a character property (props.link) and never fetches it; the workspace has no network dependency. With no url it only queues the link dialog.

Any field code is stored, but only DATE/TIME, SEQ, TITLE, AUTHOR, NUMWORDS, CITATION and TOC are updated, and layout fills PAGE/NUMPAGES/SECTION/FILENAME from memory. INCLUDETEXT- or INCLUDEPICTURE-style codes are never evaluated.
Despite labels like Show Comments, Reviewing Pane, Show Notes and Selection Pane, these only return lists of comments, tracked changes, notes or objects and open no pane.

Each runs one fixed, engine-chosen safe command through Session::run (select.word/sentence/paragraph/all, review.spelling, table.borders, para.bullets, insert.table). The caller cannot choose the inner id, so this is not replay.
